about.title: About me
about.subtitle: From business need to a working ERP
about.description_1: From June to August 2026 I worked on Odoo at KASIA Consulting, a consulting and integration firm. I worked with small and mid-sized businesses from very different sectors — phone retail, consulting, sea freight, manufacturing — from the scoping workshop through to support after go-live.
about.description_2: Before Odoo, I spent almost two years in technical customer support, then two years managing user accounts, access rights and onboarding training for new staff. That left me with habits I use every day: listen to the user, reproduce the problem, explain the fix simply.
about.description_3: My background as a developer (Java, .NET, Vue.js, React, SQL) lets me go beyond configuration when needed: Python modules, XML views, QWeb reports, data imports and checks in PostgreSQL.

mobile-money.name: Mobile Money payments at the till
mobile-money.context: In Madagascar, a large share of in-store sales are paid with MVola, Orange Money or Airtel Money. Without a transaction reference captured at the till, payments can't be reconciled with the operator's statement.
functional: Transaction reference required for every Mobile Money payment, payer phone mandatory or optional depending on the setting, both printed on the receipt.
Detection of references already used, with three behaviours to choose from: allow, warn or block.
Import of the operator statement and automatic matching: confirmed payments, amount differences, missing from the statement, not recorded at the till.
Control report for the manager to sign.
technical: Two Odoo 19 modules: till entry (OWL, also works offline) and reconciliation (models, import wizard, QWeb report).
Reads CSV, XLSX and XLS statements, with import profiles tailored to each operator.
Automated Python tests and a UI test, French translation.

shots.reference-entry: The till asks for the Mobile Money transaction number at payment time; the payer number is optional.
shots.reused-reference: A reference already used on another sale triggers a warning before validation.
shots.statement-missing: The operator statement is matched with till payments: missing, not in POS, differences and confirmed.
shots.amount-differences: Tab listing differences between the amount received by the operator and the amount recorded at the till.
shots.control-report: Printable control report: summary by result, then detail of missing, unrecorded and mismatched payments.

phone-retail.name: Inventory and POS for a phone retailer
phone-retail.context: A retailer of imported phones, with several shops, needs to track every single device — IMEI, storage, colour, battery health, warranty — from purchase to sale, including transfers between shops.
functional: Scoping with the client: purchases in foreign currency, FIFO valuation, warehouses, resellers, payment methods (card terminal, cash, Mobile Money).
Configuration of purchase, multi-shop inventory, point of sale and invoicing.
Acceptance testing with the client and user training.
technical: Tracking by IMEI with each device's specifications, Excel import of incoming shipments and purchase orders.
Transfers between shops by IMEI scan, with a mark-up scale.
Point of sale: IMEI scan, availability check and price locking.
Custom invoice listing device specifications, phone trade-in and exchange, margin reports per point of sale.

shots.imei-list: Phones in stock with IMEI, storage, colour, battery, cycles, warranty and sale price.
shots.pos-imei-selection: At the till, only IMEIs actually in stock are offered, with colour, battery, cycles, warranty and condition.
shots.pos-imei-scan: Scanning an IMEI finds the model and attaches the number to the order line automatically.
shots.imei-transfer: Transfer between shops by IMEI, flagging unknown numbers or devices stocked elsewhere.
shots.rfq-import: Request for quotation created from the supplier's Excel file, with the storage of each variant.
shots.invoice-devices: Customer invoice generated from the till, listing the IMEI, battery, cycles, warranty and condition of each device sold.
shots.net-profit: Sales, cost of sales, margin, analytic expenses and net profit of each shop, month by month.
shots.purchases-sales-unsold: Summary per shop and category: purchases, sales, profit, allocated expenses, net profit and unsold stock value.

consulting-firm.name: Invoicing, HR and payroll for a consulting firm
consulting-firm.context: A multi-company consulting firm wanted to invoice its engagements, manage its staff and run Malagasy payroll directly in Odoo, with documents matching its own practices.
functional: Regular meetings with the client to collect and prioritise feedback (invoices, payroll batches).
User support after go-live and handling of invoicing feedback.
Payroll configuration: salary structures, rules and dated parameters (CNAPS, OSTIE, FMFP, IRSA tax scale).
technical: Invoice in ariary with a task appendix, VAT-exempt disbursements, amount in words, French and English versions, bulk sending by e-mail.
Extended general ledger: purchase order reference, document number, label.
HR: employee IDs, professional groups, computed notice periods and alerts to managers.
Malagasy payslip, payroll batch dashboard and final settlement computation.

shots.invoice: Fee invoice in ariary: summary by section, VAT, untaxed disbursements, amount in words and task appendix.
shots.payslip: Payslip in ariary with CNAPS, OSTIE, taxable income and progressive IRSA.
shots.payroll-batches: Payroll batches with a summary of salaries, bonuses, CNAPS, OSTIE, IRSA, net pay and employer contributions.
shots.final-settlement: Final settlement: days worked, leave to compensate, unworked notice and reference average salary.
shots.employee-notice: Employee form with staff number, professional group and computed notice end date, flagged by a ribbon.
shots.general-ledger: General ledger extended with document number, label, entry reference and customer reference columns.

freight-forwarder.name: Business application for a sea freight forwarder
freight-forwarder.context: A freight forwarder managed its consolidation files in a macro-enabled Excel workbook. The goal: move its calculations into Odoo and link every file to invoicing, payments and expenses.
functional: Took over an ongoing project and analysed the existing Excel workbook.
Scoped per-file expense tracking with the Expenses app.
Internal acceptance testing, then acceptance testing with the client.
technical: LCL and FCL consolidation files reproducing the workbook's formulas, with Excel import.
Receipt and disbursement invoicing on dedicated journals, payment receipt generated from reconciliations.
Package release in proportion to payment, package retention, customer statement.
Margin analysis per file and expenses linked to files.

shots.shipping-file: Consolidated sea shipping file: packages, volume, taxable weight, freight and fees computed in ariary per customer.
shots.package-release: Package release showing the paid share of the invoice and the number of packages covered by the payment.
shots.margin: Container profitability: line-by-line comparison of re-invoiced disbursements and supplier bills.
shots.payment-receipt: Two-part payment receipt: invoice amount, already paid, today's payment, balance due and amount in words.
shots.customer-statement: Customer statement: packages left in the warehouse, amounts due and paid, collections over the period.
